clue.text: Playwright in gamble, out of pocket, losing 33%

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the word for a gamble

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

indicators.note: losing says that share is taken away from pocket, as money is lost from one

parts.note: a third of the six-letter word pocket is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A dramatist gambles and ends up a third poorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of pocket' reads as being short of money, but here 'out of' only says the letters come from the word pocket; what remains, CKET, goes in the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett, author of Waiting for Godot, was an Irish dramatist.

clue.text: Religious attire — black attire, restyled

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: restyled says the letters of attire are made over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Clerical dress made over in black.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Lettuce crops regularly denuded

indicators.note: regularly denuded means every other letter of crops is stripped away

explanation.surface: Lettuce crops picked bare at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a long-leaved variety of salad leaf, also called romaine.

clue.text: Register ultimate in danger is involved in solo climbing

indicators.note: is involved in says the last letter of danger becomes entangled within the reversed word
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lone means solo, on one's own

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the final letter of danger

explanation.surface: A climber signs up despite the extreme risk of going solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns LONE into ENOL; 'is involved in' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up, putting one's name on a register.

clue.text: Run into the last place to be seen with a musician

indicators.note: into says the letter for run goes inside the last place

parts.note: a tomb is the final resting place
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a means one

explanation.surface: A musician turns up somewhere grim at the end of a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone, like other instrument names, can stand for its player in an orchestra.

clue.text: He created unusual sculptures of the French prize winner

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
a champ (champion) is the one who wins the prize

explanation.surface: A French champion turns out to be an eccentric sculptor.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcel Duchamp made readymades such as the urinal Fountain, hence 'unusual sculptures'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Duchamp, the Dada artist, made famously odd readymade artworks.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance about Wisconsin regional capital

indicators.note: about says the curse goes round the state's code

parts.note: darn is a mild curse
WI is the postal code for Wisconsin

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a Wisconsin city.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the capital city of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Line in excellent meat product

indicators.note: in says the line goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: cracking is British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A butcher's line in superb meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted skin of pork, a meat delicacy.

clue.text: Radio travel broadcast is a promotional feature

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio travel slot that is really an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertorial is an advertisement written in the style of an editorial article.

clue.text: Guy in distress is a knight

indicators.note: in says the young man goes inside the distress

parts.note: pain means distress
a lad is a guy, a young man

explanation.surface: A man in trouble turns out to be a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a damsel in distress rescued by a knight; here the guy is the one in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The paladins were Charlemagne's knights; the word now means any chivalrous champion.

clue.text: Source regarding series to see in Paris

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a memo
voir is the French verb to see

explanation.surface: Someone cites a source on a series they hope to watch in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store from which water is supplied, so a source of supply.

clue.text: Article not entirely nasty? It gets a hammering

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for nasty loses its final letter

parts.note: vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A not-quite-nasty article that gets slated by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hammering' sounds like harsh criticism of the article, but it is literal: a smith hammers metal on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a blacksmith strikes metal against.

clue.text: Bathroom accessory excessively and thoroughly trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means both words lose their last letter

parts.note: too means excessively
well means thoroughly, as in 'mix well'

explanation.surface: A bathroom accessory, trimmed far too thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' clips the end of each of TOO and WELL, giving TO and WEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a standard item hung in a bathroom for drying oneself.

clue.text: Radical currently turning up in factory is to do marvellous stuff

indicators.note: in says the reversed words are placed inside the factory

parts.note: works means a factory

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: red means a political radical
now means currently

explanation.surface: A militant appears in the works and achieves great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses REDNOW to WONDER, which 'in' places inside WORKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To work wonders is the idiom for achieving remarkable results.

clue.text: Limited connection, with hesitation, in sexual activity

indicators.note: in says the connection and hesitation are placed within the word for sexual activity

parts.note: bed stands for sex, as in 'good in bed'
a link is a connection
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A cramped, hesitant connection made in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinkered means narrow-minded, having a restricted outlook like a horse in blinkers.

clue.text: Central Americans, ignoring expense, welcoming fine folk from another continent

indicators.note: welcoming says what remains takes in the letter for fine
ignoring means the word for expense is left out of the Central Americans

parts.note: Costa Ricans come from Central America
cost means expense
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Thrifty Central Americans entertain fine people from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central Americans' looks like a definition, but it is the wordplay: the definition is 'folk from another continent'. The removal leaves ARICANS before the F goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Africans are people from Africa, a continent other than the Americas.

clue.text: Historic Arctic vessel trapped in ice — not one spot to grow plants

indicators.note: trapped in says the old ship is held fast within what remains of the ice
not says the letter for one is removed from ice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
old means historic
the Fram was Nansen's polar exploration ship

explanation.surface: A famous polar ship stuck in the ice, with nowhere to grow anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fram was the ship of Nansen and later Amundsen, built to be frozen into the pack ice; removing the one leaves CE to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold frame is a glass-topped box where seedlings are raised and hardened off.

clue.text: Refuse to accept broadcast restricted by noise

indicators.note: restricted by says the word for broadcast is held inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering it widely

explanation.surface: A station rejects a programme drowned out by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but here it is the past participle of sowing seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to deny any connection with them, refusing to acknowledge them.

clue.text: Staff's methodology when hosting a travelling exhibition

indicators.note: hosting says the rods take in the letter a as a guest

parts.note: a staff is a rod, so staff's gives rod's
how means the method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: An organisation's staff explain their approach to running a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring show or exhibition that moves from town to town.

clue.text: Mid-20th century writer or early 20th century writer, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the writer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: H. G. Wells wrote The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: A choice between two writers from the first half of the last century.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell, author of Nineteen Eighty-Four, wrote mainly in the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: Absorption? Unusually large bog will absorb one

parts.note: OS means outsize, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: will absorb says the bog takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a moss is a peat bog
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A huge peat bog soaks up a single thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bog 'absorbing' feeds the definition: osmosis is a kind of absorption, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the passage of liquid through a membrane, and figuratively gradual taking in of ideas.

clue.text: New Zealand painter from good family, dosh liberally spread around

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the good family
liberally spread says the letters of dosh are scattered into a new order

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A painter from a good family who throws money about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberally spread' turns DOSH into HODS; 'around' puts it round GKIN, giving HOD-GKIN-S. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances Hodgkins was a New Zealand-born modernist painter who worked in Britain.

clue.text: Sharp humour a Roman Catholic displayed during disrupted Mass

indicators.note: displayed during says the other letters appear in the middle of the scrambled word
disrupted says the letters of mass are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Catholic makes a cutting joke while a church service is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' turns MASS into SASM; 'displayed during' sets ARC inside it after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting, mocking irony meant to wound.

clue.text: Chap apparently owing money gets court decision

indicators.note: apparently says the chap seems to be in debt, that is, inside the red

parts.note: to owe money is to be in the red
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A man in debt hears the court's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone owing money is 'in the red', so the chap goes inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A remand is a court order returning an accused person to custody or bail before trial.

clue.text: New Zealand writer offering sexist view of discipline?

parts.note: a sexist sees any area as a man's, only for men
a field is an academic discipline

explanation.surface: A writer from New Zealand voices a chauvinist opinion of an academic subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning split: a sexist would call any discipline a job for men only.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine Mansfield was a celebrated short-story writer born in Wellington.

clue.text: Description of power reflected in natural oscillations

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer's letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A physics note on how energy shows up in natural vibrations.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it signals the hidden letters. 'reflected' reverses RALOS, found across natuRAL OScillations.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar describes power derived from the sun, as in solar panels.

clue.text: One slow-moving bridge team to fare badly

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
to ail is to be unwell, to fare badly

explanation.surface: A sluggish bridge partnership has a poor evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is the proverbially slow creature, a byword for sluggish progress.

clue.text: Part of opera to cut from Tosca, retaining tenor's second note

indicators.note: retaining says what is left of the opera holds the other letters
cut from says the word to is removed from the opera's name

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of tenor

explanation.surface: A director trims a passage from Tosca but keeps the tenor's line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut from' leaves SCA; 'retaining' puts E (tenor's second letter) and N inside, giving SC-EN-A.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is an extended dramatic solo scene within an opera.

clue.text: Russian poet writing articles about Knight and Queen, tovarish? Not half

indicators.note: about says the two articles go round the other letters

parts.note: a and a are two indefinite articles
K is the chess notation for king; here it stands for knight, as in the honour KBE
HM stands for Her Majesty, the Queen

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first half of the word

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a knight and a queen and addresses a Soviet comrade.
explanation.walkthrough: Tovarish is Russian for comrade, fitting the Russian poet; 'Not half' keeps its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Akhmatova was a major Russian poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Awkward person puts it in propeller

definitions.meaning: a meddler 'puts their ... in', interfering where unwanted

explanation.surface: A clumsy person jams something into a ship's propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a pole with a blade used to row a boat, and to put one's oar in is to interfere.

clue.text: Temporarily stop America blocking outlay

indicators.note: blocking says the country sits in the middle of the outlay, obstructing it

parts.note: spend is used as a noun meaning outlay
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Washington halts a spending programme by blocking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to halt it for a time, as with a suspended meeting.

clue.text: Ebbing current with return of damage — metal?

indicators.note: ebbing means the current runs backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a flow is a current

indicators.note: return of means the word for damage is read in reverse

parts.note: to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: A receding tide brings back damage: is it metal corroding?
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, the element with symbol W.
